newsitem.title: USA: Black Baptist leader reaffirmed despite scandal.
newsitem.headline: Black Baptist leader reaffirmed despite scandal.

text.p: The president of one of the nation's largest black denominations was given a vote of confidence on Thursday by leaders of the group, despite being embroiled in a messy sex-and-money scandal.

The Rev. Henry Lyons, president of the Nashville-based National Baptist Convention USA Inc., was given a "unanimous vote of confidence" by about 200 of the group's leading members, the group announced.

Lyons' wife, Deborah, was charged earlier this month with setting several small fires in a $700,000 home her husband owned with Bernice Edwards, a woman convicted in 1994 of embezzling federal education funds. According to court records, the National Baptist Convention helped pay restitution that Edwards owed.

Police said Deborah Lyons set the fires, then crashed her car into a palm tree. She said she was angered after discovering the joint deed to the house while Lyons was on a trip to Nigeria with Edwards. She is free on $10,000 bond and has pleaded not guilty to arson and burglary charges.

Lyons has since reunited with his wife, and has publicly denied cheating on her or using church funds to finance a lavish lifestyle. He reportedly owns a Rolls-Royce and two Mercedes automobiles as well as the house with Edwards.
